newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Greenpeace adds legal twist to UK oil battle.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Greenpeace adds legal twist to UK oil battle.

text.p: Environmental group Greenpeace on Wednesday added a legal twist to its battle with the British government and oil industry over the future of the country's newest oil province in the deep waters of the Atlantic margin.
Greenpeace said that the Britain's 17th offshore oil licensing round is flouting European law because environmental assessments required under a 1985 EU Directive have not been carried out.

"The breach has occurred because the Government failed to ensure that full environmental impact assessments (EIAs) were carried out in the area prior to development and failed to ensure appropriate public consultation," Greenpeace said in a statement.

Greenpeace, along with the Marine Conservation Society and the Whale and Dolphin Conservation Society, on Wednesday made an official complaint to the European Commission calling for unlawful licensing to be blocked.
The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said that the upcoming British general election has delayed moves to implement the EU Directive.
"Decisions about regulations and consultation on this Directive will now lie with an incoming government," the DTI said in a statement.
But it added that licenses awarded in the 17th round include a requirement to carry out environmental assessments before development can start.
Last week the DTI announced that Greenpeace had bid against leading oil companies for all of the 22,000 square miles of Atlantic acreage available in the round.
The environmental group said it hoped to block the multi-million dollar aspirations of the international oil industry by turning the site into a marine wildlife sanctuary.
Greenpeace said it was given a deadline of April 3 to address the DTI's concerns that its application failed to fulfil the oil drilling and production criteria of the license.

"(Greenpeace addressed these concerns) today by claiming that the only license that the DTI can lawfully issue is to Greenpeace, since it is the only application designed to carry out the sort of EIA studies that the Government and oil companies are failing to do," the statement said.
